review_scope: Focused U.S. adult immediate-release oral trazodone MDD treatment with explicit off-label insomnia distinction.

sources.title: Trazodone hydrochloride · TruPharma tablets
sources.note: Full label and Medication Guide; SPL version 4, effective September 3, 2026. Representative 25 and 75 mg tablets.

sources.title: Chronic insomnia · AASM 2017 guideline
sources.note: Public primary guideline abstract via author-affiliated Duke repository; weak recommendation against trazodone for adult sleep-onset/maintenance insomnia. Full guideline text not claimed accessed.
sources.publisher: American Academy of Sleep Medicine / Scholars@Duke

paragraphs: Immediate-release trazodone hydrochloride tablets are indicated for MDD in adults. Pediatric safety and effectiveness are not established.

Insomnia treatment is outside the selected U.S. label. The AASM 2017 pharmacologic guideline gives a weak recommendation against trazodone for adult sleep-onset or sleep-maintenance insomnia; this is not a universal claim of ineffectiveness. A clinician should reassess the sleep diagnosis, comorbid depression, alternatives, and adverse effects. No insomnia dose is inferred from antidepressant dosing.

rows: Initial regimen
150 mg/day in divided doses; start cautiously and increase according to response and tolerance.
Titration
May increase by 50 mg/day every 3–4 days.
Outpatient maximum
Usually no more than 400 mg/day in divided doses.
Inpatient maximum
Up to 600 mg/day in divided doses for more severely depressed patients.
Drowsiness
May require moving a larger part of the daily dose to bedtime or reducing the dose, directed by the clinician.

paragraphs: Take shortly after a meal or light snack. Swallow whole; only a scored tablet may be halved along its score. Do not chew or crush. The selected 25 mg tablet is unscored; the selected 75 mg tablet is scored. Taper gradually when possible; do not stop abruptly.

Allow at least 14 days after a psychiatric MAOI before trazodone and at least 14 days after trazodone before a psychiatric MAOI. Linezolid and IV methylene blue are also contraindicated combinations. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may require reducing trazodone; inducers may require an increase based on response. The QT warning may favor avoiding the combination rather than simply adjusting a dose.

Trazodone has not been studied adequately in hepatic or renal impairment in this label; use caution. No validated numeric renal/hepatic adjustment is supplied. Individualize initiation and titration rather than assuming no adjustment is needed.

items: Monitor worsening depression, suicidal thoughts, unusual behavior and mania; screen personal/family bipolar history before treatment.
Serotonin syndrome can occur alone or with other serotonergic drugs. Fever, agitation, sweating, rigidity/tremor, overactive reflexes, diarrhea or seizures needs urgent assessment.

Avoid with known QT prolongation, significant arrhythmia history, torsades risk (including low potassium/magnesium or symptomatic bradycardia), and QT-prolonging combinations. Not recommended during initial MI recovery.
Orthostatic hypotension, fainting and sedation can impair driving and increase falls; antihypertensive doses may need review.
For an erection lasting >4 hours, stop trazodone and seek emergency care, painful or not. Do not wait until 6 hours.
Bleeding, hyponatremia, mania and acute angle closure are additional concerns. Avoid in untreated anatomically narrow angles; confusion, weakness, unsteadiness or seizure may signal low sodium.

paragraphs: Concomitant MAOIs, including linezolid and IV methylene blue, or trazodone within 14 days after stopping an MAOI. The reverse psychiatric-MAOI interval is also at least 14 days. QT-risk avoidance and other cautions are addressed in the warning section rather than mislabeled as formal section-4 contraindications.

assertion_source_map.card: Boxed warning · Suicidal thoughts and behaviors

paragraphs: Antidepressants increased suicidal thoughts and behaviors in pediatric and young adult patients in short-term studies. Monitor all treated patients for worsening and emerging suicidality. This product is not approved in children.

Reported trial effects include drowsiness, dizziness/lightheadedness, dry mouth, constipation, fatigue, blurred vision, headache, nausea and vomiting. Serious risks include arrhythmia, priapism, serotonin toxicity and the other warnings above. Inpatient/outpatient trial rates should not be pooled into an individual risk estimate.

Overdose may cause respiratory arrest, seizures, QT changes, priapism or SIADH; co-ingestion with alcohol or other CNS depressants can be fatal. Seek immediate poison-center/emergency guidance. U.S. Poison Control: 1-800-222-1222.

rows: MAOIs, linezolid, IV methylene blue
Contraindicated combinations; obey washout intervals.
Other serotonergic medicines or supplements
Monitor toxicity closely; reconsider unnecessary combinations.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors: clarithromycin, azole antifungals, selected HIV medicines
Exposure and arrhythmia risk increase; QT warning advises avoidance. If a necessary combination is chosen, dose reduction and close review are required.
Strong CYP3A4 inducers: carbamazepine, rifampin, phenytoin, St. John’s wort
Exposure may decline; monitor response and adjust under prescriber direction. St. John’s wort is also serotonergic.
QT-prolonging medicines
Avoid because arrhythmia risk is additive.
Aspirin, NSAIDs, anticoagulants / antiplatelets
Bleeding risk; monitor INR with warfarin during initiation, changes and discontinuation.
Digoxin / phenytoin
Check concentrations before combined treatment and continue monitoring; reduce affected dose if needed.
Alcohol, sedatives, antihypertensives
Sedation or hypotension can increase; avoid alcohol and review combined treatment.

paragraphs: Limited published observational data have not identified major birth-defect, miscarriage or other adverse outcome risks, but cannot establish absence of risk. Consider relapse and untreated depression risks before changing therapy; discuss the antidepressant pregnancy registry with the clinician.

Trazodone transfers into human milk. Limited postmarketing data have not identified infant adverse effects; milk-production data are lacking. Balance maternal need and breastfeeding benefits with potential infant effects.
Pediatric safety/effectiveness are not established and the drug is not approved for children. Use cautiously in older adults, who may be more vulnerable to hyponatremia, orthostasis and sedation.
Use cautiously because studies in these populations are lacking; the label supplies no fixed adjustment. Review interacting medicines, falls and cardiac risks during titration.
The antidepressant mechanism is incompletely understood. Trazodone inhibits serotonin reuptake and antagonizes 5-HT₂ receptors; alpha-1 adrenergic antagonism can contribute to postural hypotension.

facts: Peak approximately 1 hour fasting or 2 hours with food; meal timing changes exposure.
Extensively metabolized, including CYP3A4 formation of active m-chlorophenylpiperazine (mCPP).
Less than 1% is excreted unchanged in urine; accumulation occurs in some patients.
Approximately 89–95% in vitro at therapeutic concentrations.

items: Follow depressive symptoms, suicidal thinking, mania and adherence early and after dose changes.
Assess daytime sedation, orthostatic symptoms, fainting and falls; review BP-lowering medicines.
Review rhythm/QT risk, electrolytes when indicated, and symptoms of hyponatremia.
Monitor INR with warfarin and digoxin/phenytoin concentrations when combined; review CYP3A4 changes.
Take after a meal/light snack and follow titration directions. Do not split an unscored tablet, crush or chew.
Avoid driving until effects are known; avoid alcohol and discuss other sedating medicines.
Do not stop suddenly; arrange tapering with the prescriber. Report worsening mood or behavior promptly.
Seek emergency care for an erection >4 hours or suspected serious arrhythmia/serotonin syndrome.

paragraphs: Selected product: 25 mg unscored white round tablet (883 / O) and 75 mg scored peach tablet. Other immediate-release strengths and any extended-release product have separate labeling; their split/crush, food, dose and storage directions must be checked.
Store selected tablets at 20–25°C in a tight, light-resistant container; dispense/read the Medication Guide. Keep medicines out of children’s reach.

scope_exclusions: No off-label insomnia dose recommended. Guideline recommendation verified in the public primary abstract; full underlying evidence tables not claimed read.
Selected label is for immediate-release 25/75 mg products; other strengths and extended-release instructions are not generalized.
No fixed renal/hepatic adjustment inferred: label notes absent studies and cautions use.

resolved_source_findings.detail: Medication Guide describes reported priapism >6 hours; full section 5.6 directs immediate discontinuation/emergency care for erection >4 hours, painful or not. Profile uses the action threshold of >4 hours.
Selected label calls trazodone an SSRI in some passages but also verifies 5-HT2 antagonism in 12.1/12.2. Profile names the serotonin-antagonist/reuptake-inhibitor class and describes both actions.

clinical_review: Every published clinical card reviewed against full relevant primary label sections. Source-reviewed within stated scope; not an independent clinician sign-off.
blueprint: Immutable APAP eight sections, title/order, essential safety, three hero facts, cited disclosures; safety core warning/contraindication/boxed/adverse order preserved.
